data_section_full_text:
FRR No. 56 requires disclosures about audit fees, financial information
system design and implementation fees, and other non-audit service fees
in proxy statements filed after February 4, 2001. We obtain audit and nonaudit fee data from either preliminary or definitive proxy statements filed
from the beginning of January 2001 to the end of August 2001, using the
search phrases “audit fees” or “auditor fees” in the Edgar Online database for
firms with required financial disclosure and stock price data (i.e., to ensure
a timely process of audit fee data collection only for firms with available
data). We begin our data collection as of January 1, 2001, in case of early
adoption of FRR No. 56 by some firms.

We do not collect audit fee data on firms whose equity is traded as either an American or Global Depository Receipt (ADRs or GDRs) because
those firms generally do not file proxy statements with the SEC that include audit fee disclosures. Finally, we exclude audit and non-audit fee data
about fiscal year-ends other than 2000 because we require one-year-ahead
financial disclosures. We obtain financial statement data from Standard &
Poor’s 2001 Compustat Industrial and Research files ( Primary, Supplemental,
Tertiary ; Full-Coverage ; Industrial Research ). To supplement the financial disclosure data in Compustat, we also obtain financial disclosure data from the
Compact Disclosure-SEC database. We obtain stock price data from 2001
Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP) database.

The initial sample consists of 3,237 observations for which (1) proxy statements include fiscal year 2000 audit and non-audit fees paid; (2) financial
disclosures for the two previous, current, and subsequent fiscal years (1998–
2001) are available in either the 2001 Compustat or Compact Disclosure-SEC
databases; and (3) stock price data are available in the 2001 CRSP database.

aThe sample includes firms disclosing fiscal year 2000 audit and non-audit fee data in proxy statements
filed at the SEC from January 1 to August 31, 2001. The initial sample consists of 3,237 observations for
which (1) proxy statements report fiscal year 2000 audit and nonaudit fees; (2) financial disclosures for the
two previous, current, and subsequent fiscal years (1998 to 2001) are available in either the 2001 Compustat
or Compact Disclosure-SEC databases; and (3) stock price data are available in the 2001 CRSP database.
We eliminate 571 observations for firms in the financial services industry because of lack of comparability
of included financial statement data used as determinants in audit and nonaudit pricing models. The final
sample consists of 2,666 observations. The Compustat firms are those obtained from the 2001 database with
required financial statement data.
